findings.description: TypeError on Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar — Every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar crashes, because `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty. Use optional chaining with `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

Collective hosts' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none — When neither the event type nor `organizerUser` has a destination calendar, `destinationCalendar` is `null`, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing. Default to `[]`, or assign `teamDestinationCalendars` when the array is missing.

Org `slug` condition inverted: set only when team billing is enabled — This reverses the previous behavior: with billing on, the org gets its final `slug` before payment, and with billing off, it gets none. Restore the `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` check for `slug` and keep `requestedSlug` only when billing is enabled.
Video booking references lose their credentialId — Use `result.credentialId` for both calendar and non-calendar results.

Update fallback compares externalId to a falsy id, so calendarId is always undefined — This branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `find` never matches, updates get no `calendarId`, and the old destination-calendar fallback is lost. Fall back to the destination calendar's `externalId` (first entry or the one matching this credential), then `primary`.

**Also found in:**
- `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317`

Recurring calendar deletes repeat for every calendar reference — Because the block ignores the current `reference`, it deletes every remaining booking's event across all `_calendar` credentials once per reference. This repeats API calls and still uses only each booking's first `_calendar` reference.

Team admins who are not owners are wrongly denied adding guests — `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles, so also requiring `isTeamOwner` with `&&` gives FORBIDDEN to admins who aren't owners. Use `||`, or call `isTeamAdmin` on its own.

Blacklisted guest emails bypass filter via case differences — A blacklisted address typed in another case, like `Bad@X.com`, still receives booking emails because `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entries are lowercased but `guest` is not. Lowercase `guest` before both the blacklist check and the attendee-duplicate check.

Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's — When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the external calendar event is never updated, or the update throws, because `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` lacks access to the organizer's calendar. Build `EventManager` from `booking.user.credentials` instead.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered guests, so existing attendees get new invites — Existing attendees included in the request get a full 'scheduled' invite instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the raw `guests` input.

Unbounded `guests` array allows mass email spam via addGuests — Any booking attendee can submit thousands of addresses, making the server create attendee rows and email each one, which turns the mail sender into a spam tool. Add a `.max()` limit to the `guests` array.

Sync-mode token refresh returns a raw `Response` that callers cannot use — Google reads `res.data`, HubSpot reads `expiresIn`/`accessToken`, and Zoho reads `tokenInfo.data`, so token refresh crashes or saves undefined values whenever `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set. Return parsed JSON in a shape every caller can use, or adapt each caller to parse the `Response`.

Google credential key saved as the zod safeParse result, not its data — Saving the whole `SafeParseReturn` from `parseRefreshTokenResponse` makes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fail later, which breaks the Google credential. Check `key.success` and persist `key.data` instead.

Missing refresh_token replaced with placeholder that overwrites stored token — Office365 (spreading `tokenResponse.data`) and Zoom (assigning `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token`) save the placeholder over the real token, so the next refresh fails and the credential breaks permanently. Leave `refresh_token` unset and let callers keep the stored value.

Credential ID passed as userId to refreshOAuthTokens — In sync mode the endpoint receives `credentialId` as `calcomUserId` and returns tokens for the wrong user, or none. Pass the credential's `userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead.

`prisma` is used in the Salesforce client without being imported — Building the Salesforce client fails with a ReferenceError or type error because `prisma` is never imported in this file. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`.

Token refresh fails on success when `statusText` is not "OK" — On HTTP/2, `statusText` can be empty, and it can differ from "OK" on success, so the client throws even when the refresh worked. Check `response.ok` instead.

jsforce connection uses stale access token instead of refreshed one — The refresh has no effect because the connection still uses the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `instance_url`. Build it from `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` and its `instance_url`.

Computed keys collapse to "[object Object]" so token fields are stripped — Because `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to "[object Object]", `z.object` strips `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and other fields in sync mode, and Zoom computes a NaN `expiry_date`. Call `.passthrough()` on `z.object({ access_token: z.string() })` or define the expiry fields explicitly.

Salesforce token is refreshed and saved on every service construction — Each `SalesforceCalendarService` construction adds a Salesforce call and a DB write to every booking, even with a valid token, and can hit Salesforce rate limits. Refresh only when the token is expired, or rely on jsforce's built-in refresh.

Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==` — A plain `!==` leaks timing information on an endpoint that can write any user's third-party credentials. Compare against `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after checking the lengths match.

Malformed webhook body returns unhandled 500 instead of 400 — Because `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` throws, a malformed request comes back as an unhandled 500. Use `safeParse` and return 400 when it fails.

Unhandled decrypt/JSON.parse failure causes 500 instead of 400 — When decryption fails or the plaintext isn't valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt` or `JSON.parse` throws uncaught and the webhook returns a 500 with no useful error. Wrap both in try/catch and return 400.

Locked SMS accounts count as retries, so their reminders get deleted — When `isLockedForSMSSending` makes `twilio.scheduleSMS` return undefined, this branch still increments `retryCount`, so the reminder is permanently deleted after two cron runs even if the account is later unlocked. Increment `retryCount` only for real delivery failures, not intentional locks.

Temporary SMS scheduling errors count toward reminder deletion — A `checkSMSRateLimit` rejection or brief Twilio/network outage still increments `retryCount`, so two such failures delete a valid reminder that would have succeeded later. Increment only for permanent failures, such as Twilio invalid-number error codes, and let temporary errors retry.

Unguarded retryCount update in catch block aborts remaining reminders on failure — If `prisma.workflowReminder.update` throws here (e.g., P2025 when the record was deleted concurrently), the handler rejects and every remaining reminder in this run is skipped. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`, which doesn't throw when no row matches.

Unindexed `retryCount` OR branch forces a full WorkflowReminder table scan — No index in `schema.prisma` covers `retryCount`, so every cron run scans the whole `WorkflowReminder` table. Add the `WorkflowMethods.SMS` `method` filter to this branch so the existing method/scheduled/scheduledDate index applies, or add an index on `retryCount`.

Backup code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be reused concurrently — Two concurrent logins can both read the old `backupCodes`, match the same code, and each create a session. Use a conditional update on `id` plus the previous `backupCodes` value that rejects when no row changes, or a transaction with row locking.

Dismissing modal on backup-codes step skips onEnable and resetState — The user query is never invalidated, so the switch still shows 2FA disabled after the server enabled it, and reopening shows the stale backup-codes step. In `onOpenChange`, call `resetState` and `onEnable` when closing on `DisplayBackupCodes`, or block dismissal on that step.

Non-string backupCode crashes endpoint with 500 instead of IncorrectBackupCode — A JSON number or object in `req.body.backupCode` passes the truthiness check, so `.replaceAll` throws and the client gets an unhandled 500. Return `IncorrectBackupCode` unless `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"` before normalizing it.

Unparenthesized auth OR condition from getBaseConditions leaks scope when combined — When a caller appends a predicate like `AND "createdAt" > ...`, it binds only to the last OR branch of `authConditions`, returning rows outside the org/team scope. Have `getBaseConditions` wrap every returned fragment in parentheses so callers can combine it safely.

Raw HTML posts skip sanitization, allowing stored XSS — Feed content (unescaped in `poll_feed`) and remote pages reach `cooked` unsanitized, and `best.html.erb` renders it via `raw post.cooked`, so a compromised source can inject scripts. Sanitize `raw` with a whitelist before storing or while cooking.

Unescaped embed URL interpolated into raw HTML link allows markup injection — `url` comes from the `embed_url` param or the feed, and the post renders raw, so a `'` or `<` can break out of the attribute and inject markup. Escape `url` with `ERB::Util.html_escape` before interpolating.

Feed import crashes on items with no `content` field — SimpleRSS returns nil `content` for description-only RSS 2.0 items, so `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` and aborts the import, including `TopicRetriever`'s synchronous call. Fall back to `i.description` and skip items where both are nil.

Stray `if` after `end` makes header buttons conditional on the next output — Ruby treats the next output expression as an `if` modifier on the whole block, so header buttons render only when the logo link's return value is truthy. Replace `<%- end if %>` with `<%- end %>`.

Inline RSS feed poll on every unknown embed URL lacks a global throttle — The throttle is per-URL and the referer is spoofable, so distinct paths can trigger unbounded feed polls and outbound fetches. Drop the inline `Jobs::PollFeed` call in favor of the hourly poll, or add a global throttle.

absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs starting with // — Values like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` get rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking external links and images. In `absolutize_urls`, skip values starting with `//`.

Substring origin check lets prefix-matching origins send resize messages — `indexOf` is a substring test, so any origin that prefixes `discourseUrl` (e.g. `https://forum.example.co`) can send resize messages. Compare `e.origin` exactly against the origin parsed from `discourseUrl`.

Migration crashes when no `embed_category` site setting row exists — Default settings have no row, so the query returns nothing and `[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. Check that the result is non-empty before indexing, and guard the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup the same way.

SQL injection via unescaped host value in embeddable_hosts INSERT — A host containing a quote breaks the migration, and a crafted `embeddable_hosts` value can run arbitrary SQL. Quote `h` with `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` or use a parameterized insert.

Migrated embeddable hosts keep scheme, path and whitespace, so they never match — Entries like `https://example.com/1234` are copied verbatim, so `record_for_host`, which compares against the bare `uri.host`, never matches them and embedding silently stops working. Strip whitespace, scheme and path from each entry (for example, `URI(h).host || h`) before inserting it.

Host lookup is case-sensitive on the incoming host and rejects uppercase URLs — `URI#host` keeps the original case, so a URL like `http://EvilTrout.com` is rejected even though its host is allowed. Pass `host.downcase` as the bind value to match `lower(host)`.

`_ids` hydration crashes on null and leaves undefined entries for unresolved ids — A null `_ids` value crashes on `.map`, and ids `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve become `undefined` entries while the raw ids are deleted, since `hydrated || []` never falls back. Skip non-array values and filter out unresolved lookups, keeping the raw ids when nothing resolves.

before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil — Calling `create`/`update` without `embeddable_host[host]` makes `self.host.sub!` raise `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard the callback with `if host.present?`.

Unknown embeddable host id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 — For an unknown id, `where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil and `save_host`/`host.destroy` raise `NoMethodError`, so clients get a 500. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` or raise `Discourse::NotFound` when the record is nil.

Mobile `.custom-message` -40px margin now shifts it left after padding change — The `margin-left: -40px` on `.custom-message` in `mobile/topic-post.scss` offset the old 4em padding of `.small-action-desc`, so it now overlaps the avatar or runs off the screen. Remove or adjust that mobile negative margin along with this padding change.

Second `downsize` definition overrides the width/height variant — `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which now raises `ArgumentError` and breaks emoji resizing. Ruby has no overloading, so rename one method (e.g. `downsize_to_dimensions`) or keep a single `downsize` that builds the dimensions string from width and height.

Animated GIF downsize passes a percentage gifsicle rejects and retries after failure — gifsicle likely rejects the `--resize-fit 80%` from `downsize_instructions_animated`, so animated GIFs never shrink and the loop spawns five failing processes. Pass pixel dimensions on the animated path and break the loop when `downsize` returns `false`.

Fixed 10MB upload limit ignores configured max image/attachment sizes — Attachments over `max_attachment_size_kb` pass this check and fail only on the server, while images an admin allowed above 10MB are wrongly rejected. Apply the 10MB floor only to images, e.g. `max(max_image_size_kb, 10MB)`, and keep `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for attachments.

Oversized images are decoded by ImageMagick without a pixel-dimension check — A small, highly compressed file with huge pixel dimensions can exhaust server CPU and memory across up to 5 `downsize` passes, and in synchronous API mode this runs inside the request. Check pixel dimensions with `FastImage` before calling `downsize` and reject oversized images, or cap `convert` with `-limit`.

Public group members page shows only the first 50 members — `findMembers()` now uses the default `limit` of 50, but `group/members.hbs` has no pagination, so larger groups lose members that were previously listed. Add next/previous controls to the public page, or keep loading the full list for this route.

totalPages overcounts by one when user_count is a multiple of limit — With 50 members and a `limit` of 50, the UI shows "1/2" and `next` moves to an empty page at offset 50. Replace `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` with `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

Adding an existing group member raises RecordNotUnique and returns a 500 — `group.add(user)` inserts immediately, and the unique index on `group_users` `[group_id, user_id]` raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, leaving earlier usernames already inserted. Skip existing members, e.g. with `next if group.users.exists?(user.id)`.

Translation cache ignores per-site default locale used in fallback chain — In multisite, the process-global LRU cache in `I18n.translate` (see translate_accelerator.rb) keys only on key, `config.locale` and backend id, so one site's fallback string leaks to other sites and goes stale when `default_locale` changes. Add `SiteSetting.default_locale` or the fallback chain to the cache key, or flush the cache on change.

translate loads only the current locale, not its fallback locales — Outside a request (jobs/base.rb, `PostAlerter`, `PostDestroyer`), only `ApplicationController#set_locale` would load fallbacks, so missing keys return 'translation missing' instead of falling back. Load the full `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` chain in `translate` via `ensure_loaded!`.

ProvideAnonDBStore takes a bare int64 that no wire provider supplies — Wire generation fails because `pkg/server/wire.go` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore`, while the store is now built by hand in `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`. Drop `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and its `wire.Bind` from wire.go, or take `*setting.Cfg` instead of a bare `int64`.

Device rejected for hitting the limit is still cached and later let in — `tagDeviceUI` caches the device key in `localCache` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, so a device rejected with `ErrDeviceLimitReached` logs in anonymously on its next requests within 29 minutes. Set the cache entry only after `CreateOrUpdateDevice` succeeds.

Device limit check and insert are not atomic, so concurrent requests can exceed the limit — Concurrent requests from different new devices can all pass `count < deviceLimit` before any insert lands, pushing past the configured limit. Run `CountDevices` and the insert atomically, for example with a conditional insert or a serializable transaction.

Device tagging now blocks the anonymous auth path on DB queries — Each uncached anonymous request in `Authenticate` now waits on a `COUNT(*)` over `anon_device` plus an upsert, adding DB latency that grows with the table. Block on the limit check only when `AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`, and keep the async path with its own timeout otherwise.

No re-check of the asset cache after taking the write lock — On a cold cache, every concurrent request that saw `ret == nil` re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json` serially, slowing index and frontend-settings requests at startup. Right after `Lock()`, re-check `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` and return the cached value if set.

TestLogger.FromContext returns a new logger, so injected logs are lost — Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` logs only via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, tests injecting a `TestLogger` always see `InfoLogs.Calls == 0`. Return `f` instead of `NewTestLogger()` so calls land on the instance the test holds.

Legacy writes use request context that is cancelled when the handler returns — The apiserver cancels `ctx` once `Create` returns, so `Legacy.Create` usually gets a cancelled context and the legacy write is silently lost. Detach it with `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` before `WithTimeoutCause`, and do the same in `Update`, `Delete` and `DeleteCollection`.

Legacy update recomputes from raw objInfo instead of reusing storage result — Passing the raw `objInfo` makes legacy recompute the update against its own possibly stale object, so the stores can diverge or fail on a resourceVersion conflict. Wrap it as the removed code did, with `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res}`, before calling `Legacy.Update`.

Async legacy DeleteCollection timing recorded as unified-storage metric — Legacy latency and errors get mixed into the unified-storage metrics. Call `recordLegacyDuration` instead of `recordStorageDuration` here.

Delete success metric uses object name instead of kind as label — Each deleted object `name` creates its own metric series, causing unbounded cardinality and mislabeled data. Pass `options.Kind` like every other `recordStorageDuration` call.

Storage create failure recorded as legacy error in metrics — `Storage.Create` failures show up as legacy errors, so unified-storage error metrics undercount them. Call `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`.

**Also found in:**
- `pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:127-130`

Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key race on index creation — Without a per-key guard in `getOrCreateIndex`, concurrent misses both run `BuildIndex`, so file-backed `bleve.New` fails with 'path already exists' and memory builds overwrite each other. Add per-key locking, such as singleflight keyed by `NamespacedResource`, or re-check `b.cache[key]` under the lock before building.

Pause and Delete never render in list view when only promRule is passed — The menu still gates Pause on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and Delete on `rulerRule`, so the list view, which now passes only `promRule`, loses both actions. Support them via the prom rule's UID and group identifier, or keep supplying the ruler rule.

Missing `key` prop on `GrafanaRuleListItem` in mapped list — Without a key, React warns and can reuse the wrong component state, such as open menus or drawers, when filtered results are added or reordered. Pass `key={key}` as the `datasource` and default branches do.

Federated rule groups lose their immutability check in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` — Delegating to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hard-codes `isFederated = false`, drops the `isFederatedRuleGroup` check, so legacy views offer Update, Delete and Pause on immutable federated Mimir groups. Compute the federated flag from `rule.group` in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` and apply it to the returned abilities.

Null check for rawTokenId validates grantType instead — A null `rawTokenId` is accepted and later encoded as the literal `...:null` token ID. Pass `rawTokenId` to `Objects.requireNonNull` instead of `grantType`.

Grant shortcut check is inverted in isAccessTokenId matcher — The grant assertion rejects correct token IDs and accepts tokens with the wrong grant. Negate the `equals` check so it returns false only when the shortcut differs from `expectedGrantShortcut`.

Grant shortcut check reads the wrong substring of the token ID prefix — The real grant shortcut is never compared, because `substring(3, 5)` spans the token-type and grant shortcuts while the grant sits at characters 4 to 6. Use `items[0].substring(4, 6)` instead.

Client-credentials tokens fall back to "na" grant type instead of "cc" — Service-account tokens never carry the "cc" context the unit tests expect, because `ClientCredentialsGrantType` calls `generateAccessToken()` directly and never sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. Set that attribute to `context.getGrantType()` in `ClientCredentialsGrantType.process` before the token is generated.

Legacy V1 token exchange tokens lack token-exchange grant type attribute — Legacy token exchange tokens are encoded with the "na" grant instead of "te", since `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `generateAccessToken()` without this attribute. Set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` in that legacy path too.

Abstract `getShortcut()` breaks startup for existing custom grant type factories — Existing custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations will abort server startup, either with `AbstractMethodError` or a null passed to `ConcurrentHashMap.put` in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`. Add a default implementation, or skip and log factories without a shortcut.

Grant shortcuts that are not 2 characters create undecodable token IDs — `getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires a 2-character grant shortcut, so others, like the 3-letter one the interface Javadoc suggests, produce token IDs that fail with `IllegalArgumentException`. Validate that each shortcut is exactly 2 characters in `postInit` and `getShortcutByGrantType`.

Reader thread is never joined, so late exceptions are missed and it outlives the test — `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` can run while a `groups()` request is still in flight, so its exceptions are lost and the thread can leak into realm cleanup or the next test. Keep a reference to the `Thread` and call `join()` after `deletedAll.set(true)`, before the assertion.

Overlapping prefix/suffix counters crash substring in diff message — When the changed text repeats nearby characters (e.g. `abab` sanitized to `ab`), `sanitized.substring` gets begin > end and throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the problem. Cap `end` at `Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax not rendered by i18next — The admin UI interpolates with i18next, which ignores MessageFormat syntax, so users see literal `{0}` and `{2,choice,...}` text. Restore `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` placeholders in this admin-ui bundle.

MessageFormat placeholders won't be interpolated by i18next in account UI — The account console renders this bundle through i18next, so `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and `{2,choice,...}` show up as raw text, unlike every other key here, which uses `{{0}}`. Keep i18next syntax such as `{{0}}`, or use i18next plurals.

Lithuanian bundle has Italian text for loginTotpStep1 — Lithuanian users see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. Replace the `loginTotpStep1` value with a Lithuanian translation, such as `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:`.

**Also found in:**
- `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties:101-101`

`canView(ClientModel)` evaluates the same client resource up to three times — Filtering the client list re-evaluates every scope of the same resource per client, since `canView()`, `canManage`, `canConfigure` and the `VIEW` check in `hasPermission` each call `root.evaluatePermission`. Evaluate the resource once and check the returned scopes against view, configure and manage.

Failed login exposes the attempted user's passkey credential IDs — Because `clearUser` runs after `challenge`, a wrong password with a guessed username makes `fillContextForm` render that account's WebAuthn credential IDs, which lets anyone enumerate accounts and harvest credential IDs. Take the identified-user path only when `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is set, and otherwise fill the form as if no user were known.

IDP cleanup removes literal "alias" so test IDPs are never deleted — The 21 IDPs this test creates leak into later tests in the realm and can break their counts or cache assertions. Register each cleanup with `"idp-alias-" + i`, and change the other `"alias"` cleanup literal in this test to `idp-alias-20`.

Error IDs zipped with unordered `get_multi` results get mismatched event data — `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a deduplicated dict with uncached entries first and missing ids omitted, so `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can send Seer the wrong id, title or timestamp. Look up each event by its node id with `events.get(...)` instead.

Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds) — Nodestore error timestamps are epoch seconds while rrweb event `timestamp` is milliseconds, so every error is emitted before the first breadcrumb. Convert both to the same unit before comparing, e.g. multiply the error `timestamp` by 1000.

Hung spawn-context flusher is never killed because isinstance check always fails — Spawn-context processes are `SpawnProcess` instances, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so the check never passes and hung flushers pile up alongside replacements on the same shards. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or exclude `threading.Thread`, before calling `kill()`.

join() stops terminating flusher processes once the deadline passes — The `break` leaves the remaining flusher processes running after `join` returns. Skip only the wait once the deadline passes and still call `terminate()` on every remaining process.

Cluster-wide Redis memory queried and counted once per flusher process — All `SpansBuffer` instances share one Redis cluster client and `get_memory_info` reports the whole cluster, so each `submit` repeats the query and counts the same nodes N times. Call `get_memory_info()` once instead of looping over `self.buffers`.

Patched no-op `time.sleep` makes the flusher wait ineffective and flaky — `test_basic` patches `time.sleep` to a no-op, so this `time.sleep(0.1)` never waits and the assertion depends on thread scheduling. Poll until `messages` is non-empty, with bounded retries.

`queued` default is evaluated once at import, so all instances share a timestamp — Every `AssignmentSource`, including those from `from_integration`, carries the stale process-start time as `queued`, so anything relying on queue time gets wrong data. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets its own timestamp.

Installation ownership check skipped when Integration doesn't exist yet — A user who submits someone else's `installation_id` before the installation webhook arrives can link that GitHub installation to their own org, because `build_integration` trusts the query string. Before calling `next_step()`, fetch or require the installation sender and compare it to `github_authenticated_user`.

KeyError when integration metadata has no sender during reinstall — `build_integration` sets the sender only when state has it, so reinstalling an Integration without one fails with a 500 from `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` instead of showing the error page. Read it with `.get()` and return `error(...)` when no sender is recorded.

Unhandled errors from `get_user_info` crash the GitHub setup view — An expired or revoked token, a GitHub 4xx/5xx, or a network error makes `raise_for_status()` or `resp.json()` inside `get_user_info` crash the view with a 500 instead of rendering the installation-failed page. Catch these errors and return `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler leaves abstract members unimplemented, so it cannot be instantiated — `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` when calling `group_type.detector_handler(self)` for any `metric_alert_fire` detector, crashing `process_detectors`. Implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as no-ops, or keep the previous concrete `DetectorHandler` subclass whose `evaluate` returns an empty dict.

Monitor context returns raw config, discarding readable schedule_type — Issue occurrences get the raw schedule-type integer instead of its display name, so the readable `schedule_type` set on the copied `config` is wasted. Return `"config": config` rather than `monitor_environment.monitor.config`.
